For this, it suffices to use the following variant of Bertini’s theorem (EGA V ....) (for the composite arrow \(E\longrightarrow\mathbb P^r-Z\xhookrightarrow{\ \ }\mathbb P^r\), and \(s=1\)):

6.1.6.1. Bertini’s theorem: Let \(k\) be a field, \(\mathbb P^r=\mathbb P^r_k\), and \(f:X\longrightarrow\mathbb P^r\) a non-constant morphism, where \(X\) is a geometrically irreducible algebraic scheme. For each integer \(s<\dim\overline{f(X)}\), denote by \(L_t\) the generic linear subspace of codimension \(s\) of \(\mathbb P^r\). Then \(X_t=f^{-1}(L_t)\) is geometrically irreducible.
Let us now establish 6.1.2. By 6.1.4, and the commutativity of (6.1.5), it suffices to prove that all the local monodromy homomorphisms (6.1.3) for \(D_{\bar\eta}\)
\[ \tag{6.1.7.1}\prod_{\ell\ne\operatorname{car}(k)}\mathbb Z_\ell(1)\longrightarrow \pi_1^{\mathrm{mod}}(D_{\bar\eta}-D_{\bar\eta}\cap Z,\bar a) \]
become conjugate after composition with the homomorphism
\[ \tag{6.1.7.2}\pi_1^{\mathrm{mod}}(D_{\bar\eta}-D_{\bar\eta}\cap Z,\bar a)\longrightarrow \pi_1^{\mathrm{mod}}(D_\eta-D_\eta\cap Z,\bar a). \]
To prove this, let us remark that for every \(K\) finite and Galois over \(k(\eta)\), \(k(\eta)\subset K\subset K(\bar\eta)\), the scheme
\[ D_K\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=\!=}D_\eta\times_{k(\eta)}K \]

is an étale covering of \(D_\eta\), so that \(D_K-D_K\cap Z\) is a tame covering of \(D_\eta-D_\eta\cap Z\), whence one deduces an action of \(\pi_1^{\mathrm{mod}}(D_{\bar\eta}-D_\eta\cap Z,\bar a)\) on the scheme \(D_K\cap Z\). We take \(K\) large enough for all the points of \(D_K\cap Z\) to be \(K\)-rational, this being possible because by hypothesis the scheme \(D_\eta\cap Z\) is étale over \(k(\eta)\).

It remains to prove that the group \(\pi_1^{\mathrm{mod}}(D_\eta-D_\eta\cap Z,\bar a)\) acts transitively on the points of \(D_K\cap Z\), in order to establish the conjugacy of the composite local inertia homomorphisms
\[ \prod_{\ell\ne\operatorname{car}(k)}\mathbb Z_\ell(1)\longrightarrow \pi_1^{\mathrm{mod}}(D_\eta-D_\eta\cap Z,\bar a) \]
for the various points of \(D_K\cap Z\). Now, the action on \(D_K\cap Z\) of \(\pi_1^{\mathrm{mod}}(D_\eta-D_\eta\cap Z,\bar a)\) factors through the canonical quotient
\[ \pi_1^{\mathrm{mod}}(D_\eta-D_\eta\cap Z,\bar a)\longrightarrow\pi_1(\eta,\bar\eta) =\operatorname{Gal}(/k(\eta), \]
and the action of \(\operatorname{Gal}(/k(\eta))\)* on \(D_K\cap Z\) is the one compatible with the inclusion
\[ D_K\cap Z\xhookrightarrow{\ \ }\mathbb P^r_k\times_k K, \]

where \(\operatorname{Gal}(/k(\eta))\) acts on \(\mathbb P^r_k\times_k K\) only via the second factor. This being so, one sees that the desired statement is equivalent to the scheme \(D_\eta\cap Z\) having only one point (i.e. to its being the spectrum of a field). Now, in down-to-earth terms, this is nothing other than the following fact (of Bertini type) (where one takes for \(Z\) an affine equation \(F=0\), and one assumes that the point \(\bar a\) is the origin):

Fact 6.1.8.

Let \(k\) be an algebraically closed field, \(r\ge2\), and \(F(X_1,\dots,X_r)\in k[X_1,\dots,X_r]\) an irreducible polynomial. Then the polynomial

\[ G(T)=F(X_1T,\dots,X_rT)\in k(X_1,\dots,X_r)[T] \]

is irreducible (as a polynomial in \(T\) with coefficients in \(k(X_1,\dots,X_r)\)).
This completes the proof of 6.1.2, qed.

blocks.title: Remark
blocks.html:
Remark 6.1.9.

Another method of proof of 6.1.2, valid under distinctly more general conditions, would consist in simply making sure of a general compatibility for the "monodromy homomorphisms", saying that the composite homomorphisms of 6.1.2 are conjugate to the monodromy homomorphism relative to the generic point of \(Z\) (hence are conjugate to one another!).

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 6.1.10.

Let \(X\) be a projective, smooth and connected variety of dimension \(n\) over an algebraically closed field \(k\). Suppose that \(n=\dim X\) is even, or that \(\operatorname{card}(k)\ne2\). Let \(D\) be a Lefschetz pencil for \(X\), \(\eta\) its generic point, \(\bar\eta\) a geometric point over \(\eta\). Then the natural representation of \(\pi_1(D-D\cap\check X,\bar\eta)\) on \(H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell)\) factors through \(\pi_1^{\mathrm{mod}}(D-D\cap\check X,\bar\eta)\). If this representation is nontrivial, then \(D\cap\check X\ne\varnothing\) and the inertia group at every point of \(D\cap\check X\) acts nontrivially.

blocks.title: Proof
blocks.html:
Proof▾

If \(\dim(\check X)\le r-2\), then \(D\cap\check X\) is empty, and there is nothing to prove, given that \(\mathbb P^1\) is simply connected. Otherwise, \(\check X\) is a hypersurface in \(\mathbb P^r\) (XVII, 3.1.4), and, by 3.2.10 and XVII 3.5, 6.1.1 applies (taking \(\check X\) for \(Z\), \(D\) for \(D_o\)). The fact that the action of \(\pi_1\) on \(H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell)\) is tame was seen in the local theory, with the Picard-Lefschetz formula (XV 3.4), recalled below. Taking into account the (nontrivial!) fact that \(\pi_1^{\mathrm{mod}}(D-D\cap\check X,\bar\eta)\) is generated by the inertia groups at the various points of \(D\cap\check X\) (SGA 1 XIII 2.10), we obtain the desired conclusion. We shall use the preceding result to study now the condition (\(A\)) of (5.3.5). Let us first recall the following result (XV 3.4), an easy consequence of the Picard-Lefschetz formula:

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 6.2.

Let \(X\) be a projective smooth and connected variety of dimension \(n\) over the algebraically closed field \(k\). Denote by \(D\) a Lefschetz pencil, \(\eta\) its generic point, \(\bar\eta\) a geometric point over \(\eta\). Then the pencil \(D\) satisfies condition (\(A\)) if and only if the inertia group at every point of \(D\cap\check X\) acts nontrivially on \(H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell)\).

blocks.title: Theorem
blocks.html:
Theorem 6.3.

Under the hypotheses of 6.2, we have:

(6.3.1) If \(n=\dim X\) is odd, condition (\(A\)) is satisfied for every Lefschetz pencil for \(X\).

(6.3.2) Suppose that \(n=\dim X\) is even, or that \(\operatorname{car}(k)\ne2\). Then the following conditions are equivalent:

(i) \(D\) does not satisfy condition (\(A\)) (5.3.5)

(ii) \(\pi_1(D-D\cap\check X)\) acts trivially on \(H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell)\), and \(D\cap\check X\ne\varnothing\).

(iii) There exists a point of \(D\cap\check X\) whose inertia group acts trivially on \(H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell)\).

(iv) The sheaf \(R^{n-1}\rho_*\mathbb Q_\ell\) is a constant sheaf on \(D\) and \(D\cap\check X\) is nonempty.

(v) The sheaf \(R^{n-1}\rho_*\mathbb Q_\ell|U\) is a constant sheaf on \(U\) (where \(U\) is a nonempty open [of] \(D\) over which \(\rho\) is smooth), and \(\rho\) is not smooth.

(6.3.3) If moreover \(X\) satisfies condition (LV) (5.2.2), these conditions (i)-(v) are also equivalent to the condition:

(vi) the restriction arrow

\[ H^{n-1}(X,\mathbb Q_\ell)\longrightarrow H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell) \]

is surjective (hence an isomorphism by "the weak Lefschetz theorem").

blocks.title: Proof
blocks.html:
Proof▾

Assertion 6.3.1 follows from XV 3.4.

Let us pass to the equivalences of 6.3.2; (i) \(\Longleftrightarrow\) (iii) by 6.2, (ii) \(\Longleftrightarrow\) (iii) by 6.1.6, (ii) \(\Longleftrightarrow\) (v) by tautology, and (iv) \(\Longleftrightarrow\) (v) by 5.3.4. Finally, if \(X\) satisfies condition (LV), 5.6.10 gives the equivalence (ii) \(\Longleftrightarrow\) (vi), qed.

blocks.title: Remark
blocks.html:
Remark 6.3.4.

One sees that condition (\(A\)) does not depend on the choice of the Lefschetz pencil \(D\), but only on the (Lefschetz) immersion \(i:X\longrightarrow\mathbb P^r\) under consideration. This is indeed clear by (6.3.1) if \(\dim X\) is odd, and if \(\dim X\) is even, condition (\(A\)) also means that the local system on \(\mathbb P^r-X\) formed by the \(H^{n-1}(X\cap H_s,\mathbb Q_\ell)\) is constant, as follows from criterion (ii), and from the fact that the local system under consideration is tamely ramified at the generic point of \(\check X\) and from the surjectivity (6.1.2).

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 6.4.

Under the hypotheses of 6.2, suppose that \(n=\dim X\) is even, or that \(\operatorname{car}(k)\ne2\) and that \(X\) satisfies condition (LV). Then there exists an integer \(d_o\) such that for \(d\ge d_o\), every Lefschetz pencil of sections of \(X\) by hypersurfaces of degree \(d\) satisfies condition (\(A\)).

blocks.title: Proof
blocks.html:
Proof▾

By the equivalence (i) \(\Longleftrightarrow\) (vi) of (6.3.2), it suffices to see that, denoting by \(Y(d)\) a smooth hypersurface section of \(X\) of degree \(d\), we have
\[ \tag{6.4.1}\dim H^{n-1}(Y(d),\mathbb Q_\ell)\longrightarrow\infty\quad\text{for }d\longrightarrow\infty. \]
Indeed, we have the following precise result:

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 6.4.2.

Let \(X\) be a projective, smooth, and connected variety of dimension \(n\ge1\) over an algebraically closed field \(k\), and denote by \(Y(d)\) a hypersurface section of degree \(d\). Then there exists a polynomial \(f(T)\in\mathbb Z[T]\) such that

\[ \tag{6.4.2.1}f(T)=\deg(X)\,T^n+\text{a polynomial of degree }\le n-1 \] \[ \tag{6.4.2.2}\text{for }d\ge1,\quad f(d)=\dim H^{n-1}(Y(d),\mathbb Q_\ell). \]

blocks.title: Proof
blocks.html:
Proof▾

By (XVII 5.7.5), denoting by \(C(X)\) the total Chern class of \(X\), and by \(H\) the first Chern class of a hyperplane, we have the following formula for the Euler-Poincaré characteristic of \(Y(d)\)
\[ \tag{6.4.2.3}\chi(Y(d))=\int_X\frac{d\,H.C(X)}{1+dH} =\sum_{i=1}^n(-1)^{i-1}d^i\int_X H^i.C_{n-i}. \]
We have, on the other hand, by Poincaré duality and weak Lefschetz
\[ \tag{6.4.2.4}\chi(Y(d))=(-1)^{n-1}\dim H^{n-1}(Y(d),\mathbb Q_\ell) +2\sum_{i\ge1}(-1)^{n-1-i}\dim H^{n-1-i}(X,\mathbb Q_\ell). \]
Putting (6.4.2.3) and (6.4.2.4) together gives the desired result.
6.5. A reminder on the Picard-Lefschetz formula (XV 3.4).
Let \(S\) be the spectrum of a strictly henselian valuation ring, \(\eta\) its generic point, \(\bar\eta\) a geometric point over \(\eta\), and \(s\) its closed point. Let
\[ \rho:X\longrightarrow S \]

be a proper morphism, with \(X\) a connected regular scheme of dimension \(n\), such that \(\rho\) is smooth outside a point \(x\), a point which lies in the special fibre, and which is an ordinary quadratic singularity of the special fibre.

Denote by \(I\) the inertia group of \(S\) at \(s\). We know (XV 3.4) that \(I\) acts trivially on \(H^i(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell)\) for \(i\ne n-1\), and that its action on \(H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell)\) is given by the following formulas:

6.5.1. If \(n=2m+1\), then \(I\) acts through a quotient isomorphic to \(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z\) (NB. if \(\operatorname{car}.k\ne2\), there is only one such quotient). There exists an element \(\delta\in H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell(m))\), uniquely determined up to sign, which is called the vanishing cycle at the point \(s\), such that we have
\[ \tag{6.5.1.1}\delta.\delta=(-1)^m2\quad\text{in }H^{2n-2}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell(n-1)) \simeq\mathbb Q_\ell, \]
(6.5.2.2) the nontrivial element \(\sigma\) of \(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z\) acts on \(H^i(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell)\) by the reflection
\[ \sigma x=x-(-1)^m(x\delta)\delta. \]

[The element \(x.\delta\) lies in \(H^{2n-2}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell(m))\simeq \mathbb Q_\ell(-m)\), so the product \((x.\delta)\delta\) defines an element of \(H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell)\).]

6.5.2. If \(n=2m+2\), then \(I\) acts through its canonical quotient \(\mathbb Z_\ell(1)\). There exists an element \(\delta\in H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell(m))\), an element canonically determined up to sign and which is called the vanishing cycle at the point \(s\), such that \(\sigma\in\mathbb Z_\ell(1)\) acts on \(x\in H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell)\) by the transvection
\[ \tag{6.5.2.1}\sigma(x)=x-(-1)^m\sigma.(x.\delta)\delta. \]

[The product \(x.\delta\) lies in \(H^{2n-2}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell(m))\simeq \mathbb Q_\ell(-m-1)\), so its product with \(\sigma\in\mathbb Z_\ell(1)\) defines an element \(\sigma.(x.\delta)\in\mathbb Q_\ell(-m)\), and this element, multiplied by \(\delta\in H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell(m))\), gives the element \(\sigma.(x.\delta)\delta\in H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell)\).]
Let us return to the global case:

blocks.title: Theorem
blocks.html:
Theorem 6.6.

Let \(X\) be a projective smooth and connected variety of dimension \(n\) over an algebraically closed field \(k\). Suppose that \(n\) is even or \(\operatorname{car}k\ne2\). Let \(D\) be a Lefschetz pencil for \(X\), \(\eta\) its generic point, \(\bar\eta\) a geometric point over \(\eta\), and \(s_1,\dots,s_N\) the points of \(D\cap\check X\). Choose for each \(i\) an isomorphism \(\ell_i\) between \(\bar\eta\) and the geometric generic point of \(S_i=\) the strict henselization of \(D\) at \(s_i\), so that the inertia group \(I_i\) of \(\delta_i\) at \(S_i\) acts on \(H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell(j))\) and defines the vanishing cycle (6.5) at \(s_i\)

\[ \delta_i\in H^{n-1}(X,\mathbb Q_\ell(m)),\qquad m=\begin{cases} \dfrac{n-1}2&\text{if }n\text{ odd}\\[1ex] \dfrac n2-1&\text{if }n\text{ even}. \end{cases} \]

Suppose that the \(\ell_i\) are chosen in such a way that the \(I_i\subset\pi=\pi_1^{\mathrm{mod}}(D-D\cap\check X,\bar\eta)\) topologically generate the group \(\pi_1\) (which is possible, by virtue of SGA 1 XIII 2.10). This being so, we have:

6.6.1. If \(X\) satisfies condition (LV), the vanishing cohomology space \(E^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell(m))\) (\(\overset{\mathrm{dfn}}{=\!=}\) the orthogonal of \(H^{n-1}(X,\mathbb Q_\ell(m))\) in \(H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell(m))\), cf. 5.4.4) is generated by the vanishing cycles \(\delta_i\), \(i=1,\dots,N\).

6.6.2. The vanishing cycles \(\delta_i\) are conjugate, up to sign, under the global monodromy group \(\pi_1(D-D\cap\check X)\).

blocks.title: Proof
blocks.html:
Proof▾

To prove 6.6.1, let us note that, by the Picard-Lefschetz formula 6.5, we have, setting \(\pi=\pi_1(D-D\cap\check X)\), and thanks to the fact that the \(I_i\) generate \(\pi\):

\[ \tag{6.6.3}H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell(m))^\pi= \begin{array}[t]{l}\text{the orthogonal in }H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell(m))\\ \text{of the subspace generated by the }\delta_i.\end{array} \]
By 5.6.10, we have
\[ \tag{6.6.4}H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell(m))^\pi= \operatorname{Im}(H^{n-1}(X,\mathbb Q_\ell(i))), \]
so that, taking the orthogonals of the two sides of (6.6.3), we find 6.6.1.

To prove 6.6.2, one simply remarks that the vanishing cycle \(\delta_i\) is determined up to sign by the representation of the inertia group at \(s_i\). So one has only to apply 6.1.2, which gives the conjugacy in \(\pi_1^{\mathrm{mod}}(\mathbb P^r-X,\bar\eta)\) of the composite inertia homomorphisms
\[ \xymatrix@C=4em@R=3em{ \mathbb Z_\ell(1)\ar[r]&\pi_1^{\mathrm{mod}}(D-D\cap\check X,\bar\eta)\ar[d]\\ &\pi_1^{\mathrm{mod}}(\check{\mathbb P}^r-\check X,\bar\eta)}. \]

This gives the conjugacy (up to sign) of the vanishing cycles they determine, by elements of \(\pi_1^{\mathrm{mod}}(\check{\mathbb P}^r-\check X,\bar\eta)\), and the proof is completed by 6.1.1, which gives the surjectivity of
\[ \pi_1^{\mathrm{mod}}(D-D\cap\check X)\longrightarrow \pi_1^{\mathrm{mod}}(\check{\mathbb P}^r-\check X). \]

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 6.7.

Under the hypotheses of 6.6, suppose that \(X\) satisfies condition (LV). Then:

6.7.1. The representation of \(\pi_1(D-D\cap\check X)\) on \(E^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell)\) is absolutely irreducible.

6.7.2. If \(n\) is even, every subgroup of finite index in \(\pi_1(D-D\cap\check X)\) acts absolutely irreducibly on \(E^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell)\).

blocks.title: Proof
blocks.html:
Proof▾

One can evidently replace the module under consideration by the twisted one \(E=E^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell(m))\). Let \(\bar E=E\otimes_{\mathbb Q_\ell}\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell\) and let \(x\) be an element \(\ne0\) of \(\bar E\). To prove 6.7.1, one must prove that the \(\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell\)-vector subspace of \(\bar E\) generated by \(x\) and its conjugates under \(\pi\) is the whole of \(\bar E\). By 6.6.1 and 6.6.2, it suffices to prove that this submodule contains one of the vanishing cycles \(\delta_i\). But since \(X\) satisfies (LV), the restriction of the cup-product form to \(H^{n-1}(X,\mathbb Q_\ell(m))\xhookrightarrow{\ \ }H^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell(m))\) is non-degenerate, hence so is the restriction to the orthogonal \(E^{n-1}(X_{\bar\eta},\mathbb Q_\ell(m))\), hence by virtue of (6.6.1) there exists at least one value of \(i\) such that we have:
\[ x.\delta_i\ne0. \]
For this \(i\), there exists by 6.5 an element \(\sigma_i\) of the inertia group at \(s_i\) such that
\[ \tag{6.7.3}\sigma_i(x)-x=\text{a nonzero multiple of }\delta_i, \]
which completes the proof of 6.7.1.
As for 6.7.2, \(n-1\) is odd, hence \(\delta.\delta=0\), and for every \(k\)-th power of \(\sigma_i\) we have, by iterating 6.5.2,
\[ \tag{6.7.4}\sigma_i^k(x)=x+k\,\sigma_i(x.\delta_i)\,\delta_i. \]

Hence a \(\mathbb Q_\ell\)-submodule \(M\) of \(E\) is stable under the action of \(\pi\) if and only if it is so under a subgroup of finite index, because the two conditions are equivalent to the condition
\[ x\in M\Longrightarrow\forall_i\text{ such that the cup-product }x.\delta_i\ne0, \text{ we have }\delta_i\in M. \]
So we are reduced to statement 6.7.1, already proved.
